titulo: How to Learn a New Language: Sofia Balderson's 8-Step Route
caption:
How to Learn a New Language: Sofia Balderson's 8-Step Route

How to learn a new language: Sofia Balderson's route, drawn as a climb over contour lines.

She speaks seven languages, to varying degrees, and is learning Japanese now. Her eight steps run from knowing what the language is for to speaking a lot. At step 2 the ground flattens: Polish came easier to her because she already spoke Belarusian and Russian. At step 5 she says it takes hundreds of hours. At the summit, she says B1 to B2 is where you could live, work at some jobs, and have relationships. What would you learn a language for?

Source: "How I Learn Languages" by Sofia Balderson, Sofia's Notes from the Margin, 11 Jan 2026. Link: https://notingthemargin.substack.com/p/how-i-learn-languages . Her steps and her figures. Her caveat: "a strong starting point". Music: ElevenLabs (AI-generated). The retelling is ours.

She speaks seven languages, to varying degrees, and is learning Japanese now. At step 2 the ground flattens: Polish came easier to her because she already spoke Belarusian and Russian. At step 5 she says it takes hundreds of hours, and she writes "half an hour every day beats three hours on Sunday." At the summit, she says B1 to B2 is where you could live, work at some jobs, and have relationships.

alt: Contour map animation on a dark field. Lines of code settle into contour lines and the map tilts into 3D. A vermilion route climbs eight numbered waypoints; the ground flattens around waypoint 2 as the words Belarusian and Russian appear. At step 5 the camera cuts six times across the same climb under the words hundreds of hours. A held silence, then the line B1 to B2, she says, at the summit. End card: the question What would you learn a language for? and the credit.
